media.title: Flag of Morocco.svg
media.credit:
Moroccan royal decree (17 November 1915), BO-135_ar page 6 (Arabic) - BO-162_fr page 6 (French)


		
			
			Arabic-language text
		
		
			
			French-language text
		

English Translation: Cherifian Dahir concerning the distinction of the Moroccan flag — Let it be known from this Our noble decree, may God exalt its value and make happiness and prosperity revolve around its center, that, in view of the advancement of the affairs of Our Cherifian Kingdom, the spread of its glory and renown, and the circumstances requiring that it be distinguished by a flag setting it apart from other kingdoms; and whereas the flag of Our revered ancestors resembled certain other flags, particularly those used for maritime signals; Our noble consideration has decreed that Our blessed flag be distinguished by placing the five-pointed Seal of Solomon at its center, in green, beseeching Almighty God to keep it ever flying with the winds of fortune and prosperity, in the present and in the future. Amen and peace.
Moroccan royal decree (23 November 2005), BO-5378-ar page 5 (Arabic) - BO-5378-fr page 6 (French)

English Translation: Cherifian Dahir with reference 1.05.99 issued on 20 Shawwal 1426 (23 November 2005) concerning the characteristics of the Kingdom’s flag and national anthem — In accordance with Article Seven of the Constitution, the flag of the Kingdom shall be a red banner bearing a green five-pointed star at its center. The flag shall be made of vivid red fabric, opaque and rectangular in shape. The star shall be open, palm green in color, composed of five continuous points, and woven into the same fabric so as to be visible on both sides of the flag. One of its points shall be directed upward. The hoist (vertical dimension) of the flag shall be equal to two thirds (2/3) of its fly (horizontal length). The star shall be inscribed within an invisible circle whose radius is equal to one sixth (1/6) of the flag’s fly (horizontal length), the center of which coincides with the intersection of the invisible diagonal lines of the flag’s rectangle. The width of each branch of the star shall be equal to one twentieth (1/20) of its length.

leaders.name: Hassan I
leaders.note: La representación diplomática marroquí confirma la sucesión de1894. La presión comercial y diplomática extranjera no equivale al protectorado posterior de1912. Extremo anual normalizado, no fecha exacta de muerte. Los extremos de cobertura delimitan esta observación o revisión; no representan un nombramiento ni un cese.

leaders.name: Abdelaziz
leaders.note: Sucesor de HassanI en1894. Esta observación no fija una entronización31/12 ni atribuye al menor todo el ejercicio cotidiano del Gobierno; la regencia deBaAhmed necesita registro propio. Los extremos de cobertura delimitan esta observación o revisión; no representan un nombramiento ni un cese.

leaders.name: Abd al-Aziz
leaders.role: Sultán de Marruecos · soberano disputado durante la crisis sucesoria
leaders.note: Reinado desde1894; en1907–1908 su hermano reclama el sultanato. La documentación diplomática de1908 distingue proclamaciones, derrota y reconocimiento exterior de Hafid. El último extremo tiene precisión anual y no afirma ejercicio hasta31/12.

portrait.title: MulaiAbdulAziz1904 (cropped).jpg
portrait.credit: "Moroccan Bandits and the United States" The World To-Day (July 1904): 853.

leaders.name: Abd al-Hafid
leaders.role: Sultán de Marruecos · inicialmente autoridad rival
leaders.note: Ventana anual de1908, no día de proclamación: las proclamaciones regionales comenzaron antes y el reconocimiento diplomático se negoció durante1908. Firma el tratado de Fès30/3/1912; el protectorado no suprime automáticamente el sultanato. Sucesión de Yusef documentada en el primer Bulletin Officiel.

portrait.artist: J. Giry, Rue de Nimes 115, Vichy (France)

leaders.name: Moulay Yusef
leaders.role: Sultán de Marruecos bajo protectorado francés
leaders.note: El primer Bulletin Officiel reproduce la proclamación13/8/1912 y el tratado que conserva al sultán mientras somete relaciones exteriores y reformas al protector. No sustituye la autoridad francesa por una soberanía local plena.
